title: GPU Memory in LLM Training: The Ledger, Attention Kernels, and Parallelism
scope: A focused systems course on where every byte of GPU memory goes during LLM training, why jobs OOM, and which lever fixes it. Covers the six-item memory ledger (weights, gradients, Adam optimizer states, activations, the loss-head logit spike, and CUDA/NCCL overheads), the Rule of 16, full-FT vs LoRA, precision (bf16 master / fp8 / fused-CE), activations & gradient checkpointing, the attention-kernel family and its training-memory behavior (naive O(N^2) vs FlashAttention 1/2/3, SDPA backends, xFormers memory-efficient, SageAttention quantized, Ring/context-parallel, and the inference-only PagedAttention), the parallelism taxonomy (DP / ZeRO / FSDP / TP / SP / PP / EP / CP and world_size = TP x PP x CP x DP), the per-GPU memory formulas and calculator, and the OOM debugging loop. Ends in a capstone modeling a 27B 256-expert MoE budget on A100-40GB.

chapters.title: The Memory Ledger: What Fills a GPU
chapters.summary: The six items that occupy every training GPU (weights 2B, gradients 2B trainable, Adam optimizer 12B, activations, loss-head logit spike, overheads), the Rule of 16 (2+2+12 = 16 bytes/param of states before activations), full fine-tuning vs LoRA, and per-GPU vs total accounting.

chapters.title: Optimizer States, Precision, and the Loss-Head Spike
chapters.summary: Why Adam costs 12 bytes/param (fp32 master + momentum + variance), bf16 mixed precision and the fp32 master copy, fp16 loss scaling, fp8 on Hopper (Transformer Engine), and the batch x seq x vocab x 4B fp32 logit spike removed by fused/chunked cross-entropy (Liger).

chapters.title: Activations and Gradient Checkpointing
chapters.summary: How activation memory scales (batch x seq x hidden x layers), what must be stored for the backward pass, gradient/activation checkpointing (recompute instead of store: sqrt-memory for ~33% extra compute), and selective recomputation.

chapters.title: Attention and the Transformer, From Scratch
chapters.summary: The mechanism behind every memory number in this course, built from tokens up: QKV projections and scaled dot-product attention, the sqrt(d_k) variance argument, causal masking, the multi-head split/concat/W_O round trip, permutation equivariance and why position must be injected (sinusoidal vs RoPE), the full transformer-block tensor ledger (pre-LN vs post-LN, the residual stream, the 4h MLP), and the KV cache with GQA/MQA/MLA as the train-vs-infer boundary. Reconstructs Korthikanti's 34 s b h + 5 a s^2 b coefficient from first principles so each term maps to a lever.

chapters.title: Attention Is a Memory Problem: O(N^2) and Why the Kernel Decides
chapters.summary: The N x N attention-score matrix materialization that dominates activation memory at long sequence, why naive attention OOMs at 32k, the result that self-attention does not need O(N^2) memory, and online softmax as the enabling math for streaming attention.

chapters.title: FlashAttention (1/2/3): IO-Aware Exact Attention
chapters.summary: FlashAttention's IO-awareness (HBM vs SRAM), tiling with online softmax so the N x N matrix is never materialized (O(N) memory, exact), backward recomputation from stored logsumexp, and the FA1 to FA2 to FA3 (Hopper, FP8) progression and their training-memory profile.

chapters.title: The Attention Kernel Zoo: SDPA, xFormers, SageAttention, Ring, Paged
chapters.summary: PyTorch SDPA backends (math / memory-efficient / flash / cuDNN), xFormers memory-efficient attention, SageAttention (INT8/quantized), Ring/context-parallel attention (sequence sharded across devices), and PagedAttention (inference-only KV-cache paging) - how each differs and its training-memory cost.

chapters.title: Parallelism Taxonomy: DP / ZeRO / FSDP / TP / SP / PP / EP / CP
chapters.summary: What each parallelism primitive shards and its cost: DP (replica + grad all-reduce), ZeRO-1/2/3 = FSDP (optimizer/+grad/+weights), tensor parallel (split weight matrices, NVLink, TP<=8), sequence parallel, pipeline parallel (stages, bubbles, 1F1B), expert parallel (MoE all-to-all), context parallel (sequence), and world_size = TP x PP x CP x DP.

chapters.title: Memory Formulas, the Calculator, and the OOM Debugging Loop
chapters.summary: Assembling the per-GPU formulas (full-FT ZeRO-3 vs LoRA node-invariance), activation formula with checkpointing, safety margins, the allocator peak at phase boundaries (Adam states materialize at end of step 1), the debugging loop (estimate to smoke-run to read-OOM to lever), MFU/throughput sanity (6PD FLOPs/token), and offload as last resort.

chapters.title: Capstone: Modeling a 27B MoE Memory Budget End-to-End
chapters.summary: A worked end-to-end budget for a 27B, 256-expert MoE with GDN linear attention (CP=1 hard-assert) on A100-40GB at 32k seq / 248k vocab: walk the full ledger, choose the parallelism plan (EP required, ZeRO-3 expert gather OOMs), explain LoRA node-invariance vs full-FT world-size scaling, and diagnose a real OOM using the calculator as an oracle.
